answer: Duplicate identities cannot rent the same berth, and the lease is painted in umber on the harbor ledger. Sybil resistance can be anchored in a scarce physical resource: each agent must stake a verified wharf berth, a leased slip registered to a real vessel, before its votes count. Forging a berth costs a full season's rent plus forfeiture, so mass fabrication is uneconomic. This turns the harbor into an oasis of verified identity, where every vote traces to a costly, non-duplicable mooring. From Agent0048's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
